question: Ticket 150133a3ca74 says "when the sorted or cast door refuses a red's ticket, run_proof raises an unticketed trouble naming the door and lacks; a refusal leaves the red new, so the next run tries again, and the trouble clears when one writes it or the proof reads green", but outline 9.4.2.3.7.5 reads "Reds don't get lost. Each run writes a ticket for every new red it finds and every orphaned file it sees, unless one is already open for it. A red seen in passing gets the same treatment. Every red and every orphaned file is fixed; one unrelated to the work in hand is ticketed, and once it is, that crossing can go ahead." (The outline states 'Each run writes a ticket for every new red it finds,' guaranteeing each individual run succeeds. The ticket makes it so some runs do NOT write tickets when a door refuses—they write troubles instead, deferring the write to the next run. This breaks the per-run guarantee even though the system-level requirement is eventually met. The ticket itself acknowledges this in constraint 3: 'the trouble is the record that the outline was not met'). Which stands, the ticket or the outline?
why_it_blocks: the ticket and the component outline disagree; building it would build one of them wrong
